terms.gloss: an addition; something added on, an extension
terms.comment: From accēdere, to come to, be added: what is added is said to accēdere, as in accēdit quod, there is also the fact that (see further). Lewis & Short: “the thing added, the addition”.

evidence: Cic. Sest. 68: Ligus iste nescio quī, additāmentum inimīcōrum meōrum
terms.comment: Rare: once in Cicero, of a nobody who merely swells the ranks of his enemies; then Seneca (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: the adding of something, an addition
evidence: Liv. 1.30.6: Rōmānam rem nūper etiam adjectiōne populī Albānī auctam

phrases.latin: Hanc Scaurus dēmōlītus accessiōnem adjūnxit aedibus.
phrases.english: Scaurus pulled it down and added it to his own house as an extension.

phrases.latin: Quid igitur hunc paucōrum annōrum accessiō juvāre potuisset?
phrases.english: So what good could the addition of a few years have done him?

sources: Lewis & Short: accessio · Lewis & Short: additamentum · Lewis & Short: adjectio
Cicero, De officiis 1, Laelius and Pro Sestio, and Livy 1, checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) and the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
